newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's telecoms minister withdraws resignation.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's telecoms minister withdraws resignation.

text.p: Jordan's Minister of Communications and Postal Affairs Jamal Sarayrah has withdrawn his resignation, Jordan's official news agency said.
Petra news agency quoted Information Minister Marwan Muasher as saying that Sarayrah had retracted his resignation and attended a cabinet session on Monday evening.
Sarayrah submitted his resignation letter to Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti on Saturday, citing Kabariti's "haughty attitude" towards his cabinet.

Officials say personal conflict between the two men came to a head last week when Kabariti disregarded Sarayrah's choice of an acting minister during the minister's absence from the country to attend a conference.
Newspapers suggested Sarayrah had backed down on Monday under pressure from King Hussein.
"I have responded to higher wishes, which I could only obey," al-Rai quoted Sarayrah as saying.

Businessmen had dismissed the impact of Sarayrah's resignation on progress in plans to privatise the country's profitable state telecommunications body, which the minister was directing as part of the country's overall privatisation programme.

They say the move to divest a 26 percent stake in the telecomms body to a strategic partner by end of 1997 is part of an IMF and World Bank strategy which Jordan is already undertaking to step up its pace of economic reforms.
